How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment
for agenda items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per
person (six minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time
limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note
that interactions between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings
are subject to the City’s Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  C. MAYOR’S APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES –
  COUNCIL LIAISONS

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees, as well as liaisons for City initiatives.
  In addition, it is necessary for the Council to take formal action to designate the
  new Mayor to serve as the Delegate to the Los Angeles County Sanitation

  and liaisons to outside agencies and Committees.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-11 DECLARING THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL’S INTENTION TO VACATE AN UNUSED SIDEWALK AREA ALONG
  THE FRONTAGE OF 261 SOUTH MISSION DRIVE, RESERVING A PARKWAY
  DRAIN EASEMENT, AND FIXING THE TIME AND PLACE FOR A PUBLIC
  HEARING FOR ALL PERSONS INTERESTED IN OR OBJECTING THE
  PROPOSED VACATION

  Parcel A adjacent to 261 South Mission Drive has long contained private
  improvements, with alterations first approved at the June 4, 1996, City Council
  meeting using a revocable license agreement. Approval was reaffirmed with
  new ownership at the May 6, 2003, City Council meeting, which was then

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 5, 2026  3
   documented with an executed encroachment agreement and recorded in Los
  Angeles County Official Records. The agreement-term was only coextensive
  with the operation of the restaurant, which closed in approximately 2014. The
  City granted a temporary encroachment permit-covenant and agreement on
  September 23, 2025, to the current property owner to facilitate tenant
  improvements, remodeling and renovations. Based upon conversations with
  the owner, and no apparent benefit to the public of the City maintaining
  ownership of the encroachment area, City staff analyzed and evaluated possible
  abandonment of Parcel A.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-11 declaring
  its intention to vacate Parcel A, an unused sidewalk area located along the
  frontage of 261 South Mission Drive pursuant to Division 9, Part 3, Chapter 3 of
  the California Streets and Highways Code, reserving a parkway drain easement,
  and fixing the time and place for hearing all persons interested in or objecting
  to the proposed vacation on June 2, 2026 at 425 South Mission Drive.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. COMPLIANCE REPORT PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 2561

  Assembly Bill 2561 (AB 2561) requires public agencies to hold at least one
  public hearing annually to report agencywide vacancies, recruitment, and
  retention outcomes for the previous year, and discuss any challenges
  experienced in hiring and retention during the previous year and efforts to
  address those challenges. AB 2561 further requires the hearing and
  presentation to be made prior to the adoption of the fiscal year budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file this report in
  compliance with Assembly Bill 2561.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

MINUTES OF MAY 5, 2026
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Chan called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:34
  P.M. on Tuesday, May 5, 2026, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Herrera Avila.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Jorge Herrera Avila, Denise Menchaca, John Wu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Eric L. Chan.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Alex Lemieux, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief

I  Steven Wallace, Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Community
  Development Director David Sanchez, Public Works
  Director Michael Sledd, and Assistant City Clerk Adam
  Yang.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54956.9(d)(4)

  Assistant City Attorney Alex Lemieux reported that the City Council had authorized
  comm.encement of litigation.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

I  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Chan approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. MILITARY APPRECIATION MONTH

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  May 5, 2026
   Mayor Chan made the presentation and Michael Cervantes of the San Gabriel
  Veterans' Memorial Coalition accepted the proclamation.

  B. ASIAN AMERICAN AND PACIFIC ISLANDER HERITAGE MONTH AND MENTAL
  HEALTH DAY

  Mayor Chan made the presentation and Asian Youth Center Director of Programs
  and Clinical Supervisor Diana Chung and Chinatown Service Center Director of
  Programs Kerry Situ accepted the proclamation.

I  C. HISTORIC PRESERVATION MONTH

  Mayor Chan made the presentation and City's Historic Preservation and Cultural
  Resource Commission Chair Senya Lubisich and Commissioners Eric Urena and Eric
  Weeks accepted the proclamation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Denise Gotch, resident, thanked the City Council for recognizing Military Appreciation
  Month, solicited sponsorship of flags for the Plaza Park Field of Honor for Memorial
  Day and applications for veteran's names to go on the permanent veterans' memorial,
  and announced the performance of the United States Air Force Band at the Mission
  Playhouse on May 18, 2026, at 7:30 P.M.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark presented staff's request that Item 4C be approved with revisions
  to Exhibit 1 which had been provided to the City Council and the public.

I  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Wu,
  to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A-4B and 4D as presented, and Item 4C as
  revised .

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU, DING, CHAN
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of April 21, 2026.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of April 21, 2026.
  3. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of April 22, 2026.

I  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved April 9 and 16, 2026, Material Demands for the payment
  of City expenditures.

  C. MAYOR'S APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES - COUNCIL
  LIAISONS

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  May 5, 2026
   The City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-12 confirming the Mayor's
  appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates and liaisons to
  outside agencies and Committees.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-11 DECLARING THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL'S INTENTION TO VACATE AN UNUSED SIDEWALK AREA ALONG THE
  FRONTAGE OF 261 SOUTH MISSION DRIVE, RESERVING A PARKWAY DRAIN
  EASEMENT. AND FIXING THE TIME AND PLACE FOR A PUBLIC HEARING FOR
  ALL PERSONS INTERESTED IN OR OBJECTING THE PROPOSED VACATION

I  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-11 declaring its intention to vacate
  Parcel A, an unused sidewalk area located along the frontage of 261 South Mission
  Drive pursuant to Division 9, Part 3, Chapter 3 of the California Streets and
  Highways Code, reserving a parkway drain easement, and fixing the time and place
  for hearing all persons interested in or objecting to the proposed vacation on June
  2, 2026 at 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. COMPLIANCE REPORT PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 2561

  Mayor Chan opened the public hearing.

  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Macias made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that temporary overhires have been very beneficial
  and are not reflected in the Vacancy Report.

I  There was no public comment.

  Mayor Chan closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included outdated workplace policies, follow-up with applicants, time
  to hire from start to end, and that there is no preferential hiring for San Gabriel
  residents.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Ding, seconded by Council Member Herrera
  Avila, to receive and file the report in compliance with Assembly Bill 2561.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU, DING, CHAN
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

I  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto invited the community to Fire Service Day at Fire Station 51
  on May 9, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and a Community City Budget Meeting to be held on
  May 14, 2026, at 6:00 P.M. at Blossom Market.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 4  May 5, 2026
   9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Menchaca wished a Happy Mother's Day to all mothers and motherly
  figures; wished all a Happy Cinco de Mayo; and reported on another successful
  Farmers' Market, the 9th Cinco de Mayo Mercado, the grand opening of Baking with
  lsh, and that the Mission Playhouse had been featured by Desmond Shaw on CBS Los
  Angeles.

  Council Member Herrera Avila reported on his attendance at the grand opening of

I  Baking with lsh and at the San Gabriel Farmers' Market.

  Vice Mayor Ding reported on his attendance at the City Council's Budget Study
  meeting, an individual City budget meeting, Herald Christian Center Prayer Walkathon,
  San Gabriel's Farmers' Market, grand opening of Baking with lsh, soft opening of
  Mumoo Cafe, a San Gabriel Mission Playhouse strategy meeting, and San Gabriel's
  Cinco de Mayo event; wished all a happy Cinco de Mayo; and announced the Thanks
  U.S.A. Healthcare Fair & AAPI Heritage Celebration to be held on May 9, 2026, at the
  Mission Playhouse.

  Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at the grand opening/ribbon cutting for
  Baking with lsh at Blossom Market Food Hall, San Gabriel Cinco de Mayo Mercado,
  and Iris Interactive event at the Grapevine Arbor.

  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:55 P.M.
